title.narrative: ROAS: Strengthening data systems to improve the management of internally displaced persons referral systems in Iraq

description.narrative:
This project recognizes the unique challenges faced by vulnerable IDPs in accessing solutions pathways and governmental assistance aimed at supporting these. Strengthening data systems becomes a key enabler for enhancing access to governmental assistance, including MoMD grants and assistance, and social safety nets, particularly for IDPs with heightened vulnerability such as female headed households and unaccompanied minors. Recognizing these specific gender and age-based barriers and vulnerabilities, the project will also seek to ensure gendered data and analysis is included in government data, through dedicated efforts in support of gender mainstreaming with a focus to addressing barriers preventing women and girls from accessing services. As such, this project directly aligns with the DS Roadmap’s priorities of pushing to bridge documentation and compensation gaps, thereby ensuring that individuals without proper identification are not excluded from vital support.
Furthermore, this initiative seeks to empower the displaced population by incorporating their insights into the design process. The programme team plans to conduct consultations with IDPs and their representatives, creating a space for them to share their experiences during registration and accessing services. This participatory approach, coupled with a comprehensive capacity assessment of existing systems, will provide valuable inputs to target referral bottlenecks, and enhance the capacity of the Ministry of Migration and Displacement (MoMD). The broad goal is to enable MoMD's data systems to better analyse needs, inform policies, and facilitate increased access to government services. By addressing barriers to return and increasing transparency in the government database, both IOM and UN-Habitat envision a more responsive and inclusive approach to supporting internally displaced individuals in Iraq.
This action will support objective 1 of the IDSF and mobilize GoI’s capacity to improve solutions financing frameworks, which aligns with objective 3 of the IDSF. While this action is supported directly by two PUNOs, it will operate under the principle of the roadmap to accelerate solutions, which is a multi-agency framework with a monitoring and accountability framework (objective 2).
This action aims to fortify the capacity of MoMD, focusing on improved data-management, inter-ministerial coordination, and technical oversight to better assess and plan for the roadmap’s implementation. Further, in light of the GoI’s announced Plan for Camp Closures, this action will reinforce fragile yet present momentum within the government for an evidence-based plan and implementation. This effort requires a strengthening of the linkages between GoI data systems, durable solutions frameworks and policy to foster effective and sustainable responses.
The goal of supporting the capacity of MoMD is to catalyse a multi-sectoral solutions strategy and to fortify a central actor in the inter-ministerial engagement on solutions for IDPs. This action intends to improve the ministry’s ability to prioritize its response, to better advocate for resourcing, and to foster evidence-driven inter-governmental collaboration. Through this action, MoMD will be positioned to usher in improvements in planning, service delivery, and emergency response capability – built upon a backbone of quality data and analysis systems. This action will capitalize on recent actions (e.g. recent camp assessments) within the ministry to improve data systems, better inform policy through evidence, and strongly advocate for resourcing of IDP response through a needs-driven approach, with potential cascading affects through inter-governmental advocacy and collaboration.
Proposed interventions will: • Improve displacement and solutions related national data (collected by MoMD, MoP/Central Statistics Organization (CSO) in Baghdad and the Joint Crisis Coordination Center (JCC) in KRI) to empower the GoI to better formulate, advocate, and resource durable solutions pathways, leading to a referral system that enables swifter entry of IDPs into existing government schemes and programmes in their point of displacement. • Strengthen housing land and property rights (HLP) and compensation. The resolution of HLP issues is critical to enabling access to other rights and entitlements such as Compensation.
As such, IOM and UN-Habitat propose an integrated effort with the following objective: Strengthen the data systems of the Government of Iraq to improve the management of internally displaced persons (IDP) cases and enhance data analysis for informed policymaking, resource allocation, and responsive capacity, ultimately supporting more effective and targeted service delivery to vulnerable populations.
Achievement of the project objective is conditioned to the realization of the following Outcome: The Government of Iraq has enhanced data management and referral systems for internally displaced persons.
